'''Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence'''.}} [[Trade name|doing business as]] '''DeepSeek''',{{Efn|{{Lang-zh|p=Shēndù Qiúsuǒ|s=深度求索}}}} is a [[Artificial intelligence industry in China|Chinese artificial intelligence]] (AI) company that develops [[open weights]] [[large language model]]s (LLMs). Based in [[Hangzhou]], [[Zhejiang]], DeepSeek is owned and funded by [[High-Flyer]], a Chinese [[hedge fund]]. 

== Background ==
DeepSeek was founded in July 2023 by [[Liang Wenfeng]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 January 2025 |author-first1=Ben |author-last1=Jiang |title=Beijing puts spotlight on China's new face of AI, DeepSeek's Liang Wenfeng |url=https://www.scmp.com/tech/policy/article/3295662/beijing-meeting-puts-spotlight-chinas-new-face-ai-deepseek-founder-liang-wenfeng |access-date=2025-03-04 |website=[[South China Morning Post]] |archive-date=21 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250121221843/https://www.scmp.com/tech/policy/article/3295662/beijing-meeting-puts-spotlight-chinas-new-face-ai-deepseek-founder-liang-wenfeng |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Baptista |first=Eduardo |date=28 January 2025 |title=Who is Liang Wenfeng, the founder of DeepSeek? |url=https://www.reuters.com/technology/deepseek-founder-liang-wenfeng-puts-focus-chinese-innovation-2025-01-28/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250219122827/https://www.reuters.com/technology/deepseek-founder-liang-wenfeng-puts-focus-chinese-innovation-2025-01-28/ |archive-date=19 February 2025 |access-date=2025-03-04 |work=[[Reuters]] |language=en-US |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Behind DeepSeek lies a dazzling Chinese university |url=https://www.economist.com/china/2025/02/19/behind-deepseek-lies-a-dazzling-chinese-university |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250224111435/https://www.economist.com/china/2025/02/19/behind-deepseek-lies-a-dazzling-chinese-university |archive-date=24 February 2025 |access-date=2025-03-05 |newspaper=[[The Economist]] |issn=0013-0613}}</ref> The company launched [[DeepSeek (chatbot)|an eponymous chatbot]] alongside its DeepSeek-R1 model in January 2025. 

DeepSeek's models are [[Open-weight artificial intelligence|open-weight]], meaning that the exact [[LLM parameter|parameters]] are openly shared, but the training data is not openly licensed.<ref name="gibney2023">{{cite journal |last=Gibney |first=Elizabeth |date=23 January 2025 |title=China's cheap, open AI model DeepSeek thrills scientists |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-025-00229-6 |access-date=12 February 2025 |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |volume=638 |issue=8049 |pages=13–14 |doi=10.1038/d41586-025-00229-6 |pmid=39849139 |bibcode=2025Natur.638...13G |url-access=subscription |archive-date=29 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250129122940/https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-025-00229-6 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Delbert">{{cite web|last=Delbert|first=Caroline|date=31 January 2025|title=DeepSeek Is Cracking the 'Black Box' of Corporate AI Wide Open|url=https://www.popularmechanics.com/science/a63633889/deepseek-open-weight/|access-date=12 February 2025|website=[[Popular Mechanics]]|archive-date=13 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250213051908/https://www.popularmechanics.com/science/a63633889/deepseek-open-weight/|url-status=live}}</ref> Since January 2025, DeepSeek has released its models under [[free and open-source software licenses]].<ref name="Chen-2026a">{{cite web |last1=Chen |first1=Caiwei |title=What's next for Chinese open-source AI |url=https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/02/12/1132811/whats-next-for-chinese-open-source-ai/ |website=[[MIT Technology Review]] |access-date=12 April 2026 |date=12 February 2026}}</ref> The company reportedly recruits AI researchers from top Chinese universities and hires from outside traditional [[computer science]] fields to broaden its models' knowledge and capabilities.<ref name="Metz-2025a">{{Cite news|last1=Metz|first1=Cade|last2=Tobin|first2=Meaghan|date=23 January 2025|title=How Chinese A.I. Start-Up DeepSeek Is Competing With Silicon Valley Giants|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/01/23/technology/deepseek-china-ai-chips.html|work=[[The New York Times]]|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331|access-date=27 January 2025|archive-date=23 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250123102900/https://www.nytimes.com/2025/01/23/technology/deepseek-china-ai-chips.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Metz-2025b">{{Cite news|last=Metz|first=Cade|date=27 January 2025|title=What is DeepSeek? And How Is It Upending A.I.?|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/01/27/technology/what-is-deepseek-china-ai.html|work=[[The New York Times]]|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331|access-date=27 January 2025|archive-date=27 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250127211403/https://www.nytimes.com/2025/01/27/technology/what-is-deepseek-china-ai.html|url-status=live}}</ref> DeepSeek is considered more closely linked to [[defense industry of China|China's defense industry]] due to previous affiliations of its researchers and its chatbot's adoption for non-combat roles by the [[People's Liberation Army]] since March 2025.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=23 March 2025 |title=How China's PLA is gearing up to use DeepSeek AI models in actual combat |url=https://www.scmp.com/news/china/military/article/3303512/chinas-pla-using-deepseek-ai-non-combat-support-will-actual-combat-be-next |access-date=2026-08-14 |website=South China Morning Post }}</ref>

==History==
===Pre-founding years===
In June 2015, the hedge fund [[High-Flyer]] was co-founded by [[Liang Wenfeng]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Chen |first=Caiwei|date=24 January 2025|title=How a top Chinese AI model overcame US sanctions |url=https://www.technologyreview.com/2025/01/24/1110526/china-deepseek-top-ai-despite-sanctions/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250125180427/https://www.technologyreview.com/2025/01/24/1110526/china-deepseek-top-ai-despite-sanctions/|archive-date=25 January 2025|access-date=25 January 2025 |website=[[MIT Technology Review]]}}</ref>
By 2021, Liang had started buying large quantities of Nvidia GPUs for an AI project,<ref name="FT 2025">{{cite news|last1=Olcott|first1=Eleanor|last2=Wu|first2=Zijing|date=24 January 2025|title=How small Chinese AI start-up DeepSeek shocked Silicon Valley|url=https://www.ft.com/content/747a7b11-dcba-4aa5-8d25-403f56216d7e|access-date=31 January 2025|work=[[Financial Times]]|archive-date=25 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250125094520/https://www.ft.com/content/747a7b11-dcba-4aa5-8d25-403f56216d7e|url-status=live}}</ref> reportedly obtaining 10,000 [[Ampere (microarchitecture)#A100 accelerator and DGX A100|Nvidia A100]] GPUs before the United States restricted chip sales to China. Fewer than 5 Chinese tech companies owned more than 10,000 GPUs.<ref name="Ottinger-2024">{{Cite web |last=Ottinger|first=Lily|date=9 December 2024|title=Deepseek: From Hedge Fund to Frontier Model Maker |url=https://www.chinatalk.media/p/deepseek-from-hedge-fund-to-frontier|access-date=28 December 2024|website=ChinaTalk|archive-date=28 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241228030725/https://www.chinatalk.media/p/deepseek-from-hedge-fund-to-frontier|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="CNBC 2023">{{cite news|last=Leswing|first=Kif|date=23 February 2023|title=Meet the $10,000 Nvidia chip powering the race for A.I.|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2023/02/23/nvidias-a100-is-the-10000-chip-powering-the-race-for-ai-.html|work=[[CNBC]]|access-date=30 January 2025|archive-date=29 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250129054857/https://www.cnbc.com/2023/02/23/nvidias-a100-is-the-10000-chip-powering-the-race-for-ai-.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Founding ===
On 14 April 2023,<ref>{{Cite web|script-title=zh:独家{{!}}幻方量化回应市场关注：AGI不是用来炒股的，"和金融没关系" |url=https://www.yicai.com/news/101732215.html|access-date=2025-02-03 |website=[[China Business Network|Yicai]]}}</ref> High-Flyer announced the launch of an [[artificial general intelligence]] (AGI) research lab, stating that the new lab would focus on developing AI tools unrelated to the firm's financial business.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=Xu|date=17 April 2023|title=[Exclusive] Chinese Quant Hedge Fund High-Flyer Won't Use AGI to Trade Stocks, MD Says |url=https://www.yicaiglobal.com/news/exclusive-chinese-quant-fund-high-flyer-will-not-use-agi-to-trade-stocks-managing-director-says |access-date=28 December 2024|website=[[China Business Network|Yicai Global]]|archive-date=31 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231231030712/https://www.yicaiglobal.com/news/exclusive-chinese-quant-fund-high-flyer-will-not-use-agi-to-trade-stocks-managing-director-says|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="scmp 1 January 2025">{{cite web|last1=Jiang|first1=Ben |last2=Perezi|first2=Bien|date=1 January 2025|title=Meet DeepSeek: the Chinese start-up that is changing how AI models are trained |url=https://www.scmp.com/tech/tech-trends/article/3293050/meet-deepseek-chinese-start-changing-how-ai-models-are-trained|work=[[South China Morning Post]]|access-date=1 January 2025 |archive-date=22 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250122160046/https://www.scmp.com/tech/tech-trends/article/3293050/meet-deepseek-chinese-start-changing-how-ai-models-are-trained|url-status=live}}</ref> Two months later, on 17 July 2023,<ref name="DeepSeek突传消息!" /> that lab was spun off into an independent company. That lab was named DeepSeek, with High-Flyer as its principal investor and backer.<ref name="Ottinger-2024" /><ref name="scmp 1 January 2025" /><ref name="McMorrow-2024">{{Cite news|last1=McMorrow|first1=Ryan |last2=Olcott|first2=Eleanor|date=9 June 2024|title=The Chinese quant fund-turned-AI pioneer|url=https://www.ft.com/content/357f3c68-b866-4c2e-b678-0d075051a260|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240717030903/https://www.ft.com/content/357f3c68-b866-4c2e-b678-0d075051a260|archive-date=17 July 2024 |access-date=28 December 2024|work=[[Financial Times]]}}</ref> Initially, [[venture capital]] investors were reluctant to provide funding, as they considered it unlikely that the venture would be able to quickly generate an [[Exit (investing)|exit]] (an ownership stake in an investment).<ref name="Ottinger-2024" />

==Company operation==
DeepSeek is headquartered in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, and is owned and funded by [[High-Flyer]]. Its co-founder, [[Liang Wenfeng]], serves as CEO. As of May 2024, Liang personally held an 84% stake in DeepSeek through two [[shell corporation]]s.{{NoteTag|宁波程信柔兆企业管理咨询合伙企业（有限合伙） and 宁波程恩企业管理咨询合伙企业（有限合伙）}}<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 May 2024 |script-title=zh:大模型价格又砍一刀 这次"屠夫"竟是量化私募？ |url=https://www.cls.cn/detail/1672635 |access-date=3 February 2025 |website=www.cls.cn |archive-date=27 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241227042059/https://www.cls.cn/detail/1672635 |url-status=live }}</ref> In February 2026, [[Anthropic]] accused DeepSeek of using thousands of fraudulent Chinese Companies of Harvesting Its Data |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/23/technology/anthropic-chinese-startups-distillation.html |access-date=2026-02-24 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> In April 2026, investors began speaking with DeepSeek for a $300 million funding round, which would bring DeepSeek to a total valuation of $10 billion.<ref name="Reuters funding">{{Cite web |last1=Sultan |first1=Abu |last2=Kachwala |first2=Zaheer |editor1=Anil D'Silva |editor2=Devika Syamnath |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/china/chinas-deepseek-is-raising-funds-10-billion-valuation-information-reports-2026-04-17/ |title=China's DeepSeek is raising funds at $10 billion valuation, The Information reports |date=18 April 2026 |access-date=21 April 2026 |website=[[Reuters]]}}</ref>{{Update inline|date=July 2026}} DeepSeek completed a May 2026 [[Series A round]] receiving US$7 billion, |url=https://www.ft.com/content/6deb470e-d152-43a2-be0d-cc1fde4f3db8?syn-25a6b1a6=1|date=14 July 2026|access-date=1 September 2026|website=[[Financial Times]]}}</ref> In July 2026, Bloomberg and the Financial Times reported the company had begun preparations for an IPO that would see it list as soon as 2027.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fan |first=Haze |date=14 July 2026 |title=DeepSeek Is Preparing For |access-date=2026-08-26 |website=South China Morning Post }}</ref>

Due to its open weight framework, DeepSeek models have been hosted natively by cloud providers including [[Microsoft Azure]] and [[Perplexity AI]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Forlini |first=Emily |date=30 January 2025 |title=DeepSeek Is Here to Stay as Microsoft, Perplexity Integrate Its Model |url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/deepseek-is-here-to-stay-as-microsoft-perplexity-integrate-its-model |access-date=2026-08-31 |website=PCMAG }}</ref>[[File:Deepseek login error.png|thumb|The DeepSeek login page following a [[cyberattack]] around its 21 January 2025 launch]]
===Strategy===
DeepSeek has stated that it focuses on research and does not have immediate plans for commercialization.<ref name="Schneider-2024">{{Cite web|last=Schneider|first=Jordan|date=27 November 2024|title=Deepseek: The Quiet Giant Leading China's AI Race|url=https://www.chinatalk.media/p/deepseek-ceo-interview-with-chinas|website=ChinaTalk|access-date=28 December 2024|archive-date=29 November 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241129213821/https://www.chinatalk.media/p/deepseek-ceo-interview-with-chinas|url-status=live}}</ref> This posture also means it can skirt certain provisions of China's AI regulations aimed at consumer-facing technologies.<ref name="Metz-2025a" />{{Update inline|date=July 2026}}{{Original research inline|date=July 2026}}<!-- while it may be true, there is no bridging source -->

DeepSeek operates with a relaxed, academic research-style workplace culture that deliberately avoids China’s "996" overtime practices. Founder Liang Wenfeng structured the company to eliminate rigid Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and mandatory overtime, allowing significant time for unstructured research and creative exploration.<ref>{{cite web |title=Despite China’s 996 culture, DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng says his workers don’t do overtime or even have KPIs: ‘No one manages them’ |url=https://fortune.com/2026/08/01/deepseek-founder-liang-wenfeng-workers-dont-do-overtime-or-kpis-china-996-culture/ |website=Fortune}}</ref>

DeepSeek's hiring approach emphasizes skills over lengthy work experience, resulting in many hires fresh out of university.<ref name="Metz-2025a" /><ref name="scmp 1 January 2025" /> The company likewise recruits individuals without computer science backgrounds to expand the range of expertise incorporated into the models, for instance in poetry or advanced mathematics.<ref name="Metz-2025a" /><ref name="Metz-2025b" /> According to [[The New York Times]], dozens of DeepSeek researchers have or have previously had affiliations with [[People's Liberation Army]] laboratories and the [[Seven Sons of National Defence]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last1=Mickle |first1=Tripp |last2=Swanson |first2=Ana |last3=Tobin |first3=Meaghan |last4=Metz |first4=Cade |date=16 April 2025 |title=US Officials Target Nvidia and DeepSeek Amid Fears of China's A.I. Progress |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/04/16/technology/nvidia-deepseek-china-ai-trump.html |url-access=registration |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250416175114/https://www.nytimes.com/2025/04/16/technology/nvidia-deepseek-china-ai-trump.html |archive-date=2025-04-16 |access-date=2025-04-17 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Since 2025, its chatbot was adopted in non-combat roles by the People's Liberation Army, including hospitals, the [[People's Armed Police]] paramilitary, and national mobilization organizations.<ref name=":4" />

Due to U.S. chip restrictions, DeepSeek has continuously refined its algorithms to maximize computational efficiency, leveraging older hardware and reducing energy consumption.<ref name=":110">{{Cite book |last1=Greenspan|first1=Anna|title=Machine Decision is Not Final: China and the History and Future of Artificial Intelligence|last2=Konior|first2=Bogna|publisher=Urbanomic, [[MIT Press]]|year=2025|isbn=9781913029999|editor-last=Bratton|editor-first=Benjamin|chapter=Introduction: Fleeting Forces and Clever Machinations|editor-last2=Greenspan|editor-first2=Anna|editor-last3=Ireland|editor-first3=Amy|editor-last4=Konior|editor-first4=Bogna}}</ref>{{Reference page|page=19}}

DeepSeek also expanded into Africa, offering more affordable and less power-hungry AI solutions. The company has bolstered African language models and generated a number of startups, for example in [[Nairobi]]. Along with [[Huawei]]'s storage and cloud computing services, the impact on the tech scene in sub-Saharan Africa is considerable. DeepSeek offers local data sovereignty and more flexibility compared to Western AI platforms.<ref>Rai, Saritha, Loni Prinsloo, and Helen Nyambura [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2025-10-22/china-s-deepseek-pushes-into-africa-making-ai-accessible-to-millions?embedded-checkout=true "China's DeepSeek Is Beating Out OpenAI and Google in Africa"] ''Bloomberg Technology''. Accessed 27 October 2025.</ref>

==Training framework==
High-Flyer/DeepSeek had operated at least two primary computing clusters: Fire-Flyer and Fire-Flyer 2. Fire-Flyer 1 was constructed in 2019 and was retired after 1.5 years of operation.{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}} Fire-Flyer 2 is still in operation as of 2025.{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}} Fire-Flyer 2 consists of co-designed software and hardware architecture.{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}} On the hardware side, Nvidia GPUs use 200 [[Data-rate units|Gbps]] interconnects.{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}} The cluster is divided into two zones, and the platform supports cross-zone tasks.{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}} The [[network topology]] consisted of two [[fat tree]]s, chosen for their high [[bisection bandwidth]]. On the software side, there are:<ref name="DL">{{Cite book|last1=An|first1=Wei|last2=Bi|first2=Xiao |last3=Chen|first3=Guanting|last4=Chen|first4=Shanhuang|last5=Deng|first5=Chengqi|last6=Ding|first6=Honghui|last7=Dong|first7=Kai|last8=Du|first8=Qiushi|last9=Gao|first9=Wenjun|last10=Guan|first10=Kang|last11=Guo|first11=Jianzhong|last12=Guo|first12=Yongqiang|last13=Fu|first13=Zhe|last14=He|first14=Ying|last15=Huang|first15=Panpan |chapter=Fire-Flyer AI-HPC: A Cost-Effective Software-Hardware Co-Design for Deep Learning |date=17 November 2024|title=SC24: International Conference for High Performance Computing, Networking, Storage and Analysis |publisher=IEEE|pages=1–23|doi=10.1109/SC41406.2024.00089|isbn=979-8-3503-5291-7|arxiv=2408.14158}}</ref>

*<code>3FS</code> (Fire-Flyer File System): A [[Clustered file system|distributed parallel file system]] designed for asynchronous random reads. It uses Direct I/O and [[Remote direct memory access|RDMA Read]]. In contrast to standard Buffered I/O, Direct I/O does not cache data. Caching is useless in this case, since each piece of data read is random and is not reused.<ref>{{Cite web|date=13 June 2019|script-title=zh:幻方力量 {{!}} 高速文件系统 3FS|url=https://www.high-flyer.cn/blog/3fs/|access-date=2025-02-03|website=[[High-Flyer]]|archive-date=3 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250203011728/https://www.high-flyer.cn/blog/3fs/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |title=deepseek-ai/3FS |date=28 February 2025 |url=https://github.com/deepseek-ai/3FS |access-date=2025-02-28 |publisher=DeepSeek |archive-date=28 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250228054402/https://github.com/deepseek-ai/3FS |url-status=live }}</ref>
*<code>hfreduce</code>: Library for [[asynchronous communication]], originally designed to replace [[Nvidia]] Collective Communication Library (NCCL).<ref name="RD">{{Cite web|date=4 March 2020|script-title=zh:hfreduce {{!}} 高性能的多卡并行通信工具|url=https://www.high-flyer.cn/blog/hf-reduce/|access-date=2025-02-03|website=[[High-Flyer]]|archive-date=28 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250128032837/https://www.high-flyer.cn/blog/hf-reduce/|url-status=live}}</ref> It is mainly used for [[allreduce]], especially of gradients during [[backpropagation]].{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}} It runs asynchronously on the CPU to avoid blocking [[Compute kernel|kernels]] on the GPU.<ref name="DL" /> It uses [[two-tree broadcast]] like NCCL.<ref name="RD" />
*<code>hfai.nn</code>: Software library of commonly used operators for neural network training, similar to <code>torch.nn</code> in [[PyTorch]].{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}}
*<code>HaiScale Distributed Data Parallel</code> (DDP): Parallel training library that implements various forms of parallelism such as [[data parallelism]] (DP), [[Pipeline (computing)|pipeline parallelism]] (PP), tensor parallelism (TP), experts parallelism (EP), fully sharded data parallel (FSDP) and zero redundancy optimizer (ZeRO). It is similar to PyTorch DDP, which uses NCCL on the backend.
*<code>HAI Platform</code>: Various applications such as task scheduling, fault handling, and disaster recovery.<ref>{{Citation |date=2 February 2025|title=HFAiLab/hai-platform |url=https://github.com/HFAiLab/hai-platform|access-date=2025-02-03 |website=[[High-Flyer]]}}</ref>
As of 2022, Fire-Flyer 2 had 5,000 [[PCI Express|PCIe]] A100 GPUs in 625 nodes, each containing 8 GPUs.<ref name="RD" />

==DeepSeek Harness==
{{Expand section|date=August 2026}}
DeepSeek Harness is an [[open-source software|open-source]] [[AI agent]] [[Agent harness|harness]] developed by DeepSeek. It provides an environment for building and running AI agents, with components including models, tools, skills, sessions, [[Sandbox (computer security)|sandboxes]], storage, scheduling, and user interfaces. The software uses Cordis plugin architecture and is distributed under the [[MIT License]]. As of August 2026, DeepSeek Harness is available as a developer preview.<ref name="DeepSeekHarness"/>

=== Plugin architecture ===
DeepSeek Harness uses an "everything-is-a-plugin" design philosophy powered by the Cordis framework.<ref name="DeepSeekHarness">{{cite web|title=DeepSeek Harness|url=https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness|website=GitHub|publisher=DeepSeek AI|quote=DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) is an open-source agent harness ... It is built on an everything-is-a-plugin architecture and powered by Cordis|access-date=29 August 2026}}</ref> This allows major agent components to be added, removed, or reloaded while the software is running.<ref name="DeepSeekHarness"/><ref name="NewStackDeepSeek">{{cite web|last=Lardinois|first=Frederic|title=DeepSeek open sources an agent harness where everything is a plugin|url=https://thenewstack.io/deepseek-harness-open-source-plugins/|website=The New Stack|date=13 August 2026|access-date=29 August 2026}}</ref> The modular design enables developers to switch between third-party providers or alternative model configurations without changing the rest of the system.<ref name="NewStackDeepSeek"/>

==Model releases==
{{Expand section|date=July 2026}}

On 21 August 2025, DeepSeek released DeepSeek V3.1 under the MIT License.<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 August 2025 |title=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1 · Hugging Face |url=https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1 |access-date=2025-08-25 |website=huggingface.co}}</ref> This model features a hybrid architecture with thinking and non-thinking modes. It also surpasses prior models like V3 and R1, by over 40% on certain benchmarks like SWE-bench and Terminal-bench.<ref>{{Cite web |title=DeepSeek-V3.1 Release {{!}} DeepSeek API Docs |url=https://api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news250821 |access-date=2025-08-25 |website=api-docs.deepseek.com }}</ref> It was updated to V3.1-Terminus on 22 September 2025, which fixed multiple language artifacts and improved in intelligence in general.<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 September 2025 |title=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus · Hugging Face |url=https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus |access-date=2025-09-24 |website=huggingface.co}}</ref>

DeepSeek V3.2-Exp was released on 29 September 2025. It uses DeepSeek Sparse Attention, a more efficient [[Transformer (deep learning architecture)#Sub-quadratic transformers|attention mechanism]] based on previous research published in February. It was based on DeepSeek V3.1 Terminus.<ref name=":6">{{Citation |last1=Yuan |first1=Jingyang |title=Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention |date=27 February 2025 |arxiv=2502.11089 |last2=Gao |first2=Huazuo |last3=Dai |first3=Damai |last4=Luo |first4=Junyu |last5=Zhao |first5=Liang |last6=Zhang |first6=Zhengyan |last7=Xie |first7=Zhenda |last8=Wei |first8=Y. X. |last9=Wang |first9=Lean}}</ref><ref name=":7">{{Cite web |date=29 September 2025 |title=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp · Hugging Face |url=https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp |access-date=2025-10-02 |website=huggingface.co}}</ref> DeepSeek-V3.2 was released on 1 December 2025, alongside a DeepSeek-V3.2-Speciale variant that focused on reasoning.<ref name="Binder-2025">{{cite web |last1=Binder |first1=Matt |title=DeepSeek v3.2: What it is, how it compares to ChatGPT, how to try it |url=https://mashable.com/article/deepseek-v3-2-models-released |website=[[Mashable]] |access-date=12 April 2026 |date=3 December 2025}}</ref><ref name="DeepSeek-V3.2 release">{{cite web |title=DeepSeek-V3.2 Release |url=https://api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news251201 |website=DeepSeek API Docs |access-date=12 April 2026 |date=1 December 2025}}</ref>

=== R1 series ===
On 20 January 2025, DeepSeek launched the DeepSeek-R1 model, which was free for [[iOS]] and [[Android (operating system)|Android]]. By 27 January, DeepSeek surpassed [[ChatGPT]] as the most downloaded freeware app on the [[App Store (iOS)|iOS App Store]] in the United States,<ref name="Metz-2025b" /> triggering an 18% drop in Nvidia's share price.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Field|first=Hayden|date=27 January 2025|title=China's DeepSeek AI dethrones ChatGPT on App Store: Here's what you should know|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2025/01/27/chinas-deepseek-ai-tops-chatgpt-app-store-what-you-should-know.html|work=[[CNBC]]|access-date=27 January 2025|archive-date=28 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250128201052/https://www.cnbc.com/2025/01/27/chinas-deepseek-ai-tops-chatgpt-app-store-what-you-should-know.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Picchi|first=Aimee|date=27 January 2025|title=What is DeepSeek, and why is it causing Nvidia and other stocks to slump?|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/what-is-deepseek-ai-china-stock-nvidia-nvda-asml/|work=[[CBS News]]|access-date=27 January 2025|archive-date=29 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250129002522/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/what-is-deepseek-ai-china-stock-nvidia-nvda-asml/|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 28 May 2025, DeepSeek released DeepSeek-R1-0528 under the MIT License, which was a minor update upon R1. Its scores have also exceeded both DeepSeek R1 (January) and DeepSeek V3-0324 in certain benchmarks.<ref name=":2" />

=== V4 series ===
On 24 April 2026, DeepSeek released a preview of its V4 series, including the 284-billion parameter DeepSeek-V4-Flash and the 1.6-trillion parameter DeepSeek-V4-Pro. Both feature a one million token [[context window]], under the MIT License.<ref name="Sankaran-2026">{{Cite web |last=Sankaran |first=Vishwam |date=24 April 2026 |title=China's DeepSeek releases new AI model it claims beats all open-source competitors |url=https://www.the-independent.com/tech/deepseek-v4-pro-ai-model-china-release-b2964052.html |access-date=2026-04-24 |website=The Independent }}</ref><ref name="Chen-2026b">{{cite web |last1=Chen |first1=Caiwei |title=Three reasons why DeepSeek's new model matters |url=https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/04/24/1136422/why-deepseeks-v4-matters/ |website=[[MIT Technology Review]] |access-date=25 April 2026 |date=24 April 2026}}</ref><ref name="Tolomia-2026">{{cite web |last1=Tolomia |first1=Cris |title=DeepSeek is back with a new open-source AI model built on Chinese chips |url=https://qz.com/deepseek-v4-model-huawei-chips-open-source-042426 |website=[[Quartz (publication)|Quartz]] |access-date=25 April 2026 |date=24 April 2026}}</ref> V4 has been adopted by semiconductor manufacturers such as [[Huawei]] and [[Cambricon Technologies]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 May 2026 |title=China's chipmakers rush to embrace DeepSeek's V4. Which names stand out? |url=https://www.scmp.com/tech/big-tech/article/3352644/chinas-chipmakers-rush-embrace-deepseeks-v4-which-names-stand-out |access-date=2026-05-07 |website=South China Morning Post }}</ref> The official versions of DeepSeek V4-Flash and V4-Pro were released on 31 July and 13 August, respectively.<ref name="Baptista-2026">{{cite web |last1=Baptista |first1=Eduardo |title=DeepSeek's new AI model is by far the cheapest of well-known models to run, research firm says |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/deepseeks-new-ai-model-is-by-far-cheapest-well-known-models-run-research-firm-2026-08-03/ |website=[[Reuters]] |access-date=13 August 2026 |date=3 August 2026}}</ref><ref name="Gigazine V4-Pro">{{cite web |title=Chinese AI startup DeepSeek quietly released 'DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813'. |url=https://gigazine.net/gsc_news/en/20260813-deepseek-v4-pro-0813 |website=[[Gigazine]] |access-date=13 August 2026 |date=13 August 2026}}</ref> V4.1-Flash, which was made available on 10 September 2026, introduced a "causal encoder-decoder" system and had lower memory usage compared to previous versions, according to DeepSeek.<ref name="Lee-2026">{{Cite news |first=Chong Ming |last=Lee |date=10 September 2026 |title=DeepSeek says new Flash AI model beats Kimi K3 on cyber, coding benchmarks |url=https://www.scmp.com/tech/big-tech/article/3367051/deepseek-says-new-flash-ai-model-beats-kimi-k3-cyber-coding-benchmarks |access-date=10 September 2026 |newspaper=[[South China Morning Post]] }}</ref><ref name="Haralu-2026">{{cite news |last1=Haralu |first1=Kileuna |title=DeepSeek Launches V4.1-Flash to Make Large-Scale AI Inference Cheaper |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news/deepseek-launches-v41-flash-to-make-large-scale-ai-inference-cheaper |magazine=Analytics India Mag |access-date=10 September 2026 |date=10 September 2026}}</ref>

==Technical specifications of models==
DeepSeek's models are open-weight, which provides less freedom for modification than true [[open source]] software.<ref name="gibney2023" /><ref name="Delbert"/>{{Original research inline|date=July 2026}}

== Legal status ==
In the United States, the [[National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026]] instructs the [[United States Secretary of Defense]] and the [[Director of National Intelligence]] to remove and exclude any artificial intelligence developed by DeepSeek or owned by HighFlyer from devices operated by the [[United States Department of Defense]] and [[United States Intelligence Community]] or their contractors. Artificial intelligence by DeepSeek is only allowed with explicit permissions for research, training, and evaluation or military activities supporting national security functions such as [[counterterrorism]] or [[counterintelligence]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cyber and Artificial Intelligence Provisions in the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) |url=https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/IF13197 |access-date=2026-07-06 |website=www.congress.gov}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sen. Cornyn |first=John [R-TX |date=18 December 2025 |title=Text - S.1071 - 119th Congress (2025-2026): National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 |url=https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/1071/text |access-date=2026-07-06 |website=www.congress.gov}}</ref>

In Australia, the [[Department of Home Affairs (Australia)|Department of Home Affairs]] issued a government-wide directive "to prevent the use or installation of DeepSeek products, applications and web services and where found remove all existing instances of DeepSeek products, applications and web services from all Australian Government systems and devices."<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 February 2025 |title=PSPF Direction Update – DeepSeek Products, Applications and Web Services |url=https://www.protectivesecurity.gov.au/news/pspf-direction-update-deepseek-products-applications-and-web-services |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250207114054/https://www.protectivesecurity.gov.au/news/pspf-direction-update-deepseek-products-applications-and-web-services |archive-date=2025-02-07 |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=protectivesecurity.gov.au/}}</ref>
